findings.title: remove_stock underflows quantity when count exceeds current stock
findings.explanation: remove_stock validates that the SKU exists but never checks that `count <= item.quantity` before subtracting. `quantity` is a u32, so subtracting more than is in stock underflows.
findings.failure_scenario: With an item at quantity 10, calling `inventory.remove_stock("A", 11)` panics with 'attempt to subtract with overflow' in a debug build, or in a release build silently wraps to 4294967290, so the function returns `Ok(4294967290)` as if that were a legitimate remaining stock count — corrupting the inventory with no error surfaced, even though the function already returns a `Result` that could report this cleanly.

findings.title: average_price divides by zero on an empty inventory
findings.explanation: The denominator is the item count with no guard for the empty case, so an empty (or emptied) inventory triggers integer division by zero.
findings.failure_scenario: `Inventory::new().average_price()` panics with 'attempt to divide by zero'; any caller that computes an average before adding items, or after all items are removed, crashes.

findings.title: top_by_value panics when n exceeds the number of items
findings.explanation: The slice `items[..n]` is never clamped to `items.len()`, so requesting more top items than exist indexes past the end of the vector.
findings.failure_scenario: On an inventory with 2 items, `inventory.top_by_value(5)` panics with 'range end index 5 out of range for slice of length 2' instead of returning the 2 items that exist.

findings.title: parse_price panics on any malformed price string
findings.explanation: Every step uses `.unwrap()` with no validation: a missing '.' makes `split_once` return `None`, and non-numeric pound/pence segments make `parse::<u64>()` return `Err`; both panic instead of returning an error from this parsing function.
findings.failure_scenario: `parse_price("free")` panics because there is no '.' to split on; `parse_price("abc.12")` panics on the pounds parse. Any externally supplied, imperfectly-formatted price string crashes the caller instead of yielding a recoverable error.

findings.title: basket_total discount tiers are off by one versus their documented thresholds
findings.explanation: The doc comment states baskets of '10 or more' get 5% off and '50 or more' get 10% off, but the code uses strict `>`, so exactly 10 items get 0% off and exactly 50 items get only 5% off — the boundary quantities silently receive one tier lower than documented.
findings.failure_scenario: `basket_total(1000, 10)` returns 10000 (no discount) even though the documented behavior for '10 or more items' promises 5% off (9500); `basket_total(1000, 50)` returns 9500 (5% off) instead of the documented 10% off (9000).

findings.title: parse_price mishandles pence fractions that aren't exactly two digits
findings.explanation: The pence segment is parsed as a raw integer and added directly rather than being interpreted as a two-digit fractional part, so its value depends on how many digits follow the decimal point instead of representing hundredths of a pound.
findings.failure_scenario: `parse_price("12.5")` (intended as £12.50) returns 1205 pence (£12.05) instead of 1250; `parse_price("12.345")` returns 1545 pence, a value with no sensible relationship to the input.

findings.title: apply_discount underflows for a percent_off greater than 100
findings.explanation: Nothing constrains `percent_off` to 0..=100, so a caller-supplied value above 100 makes `discount` exceed `price_pence`, and the subsequent subtraction underflows the u64.
findings.failure_scenario: `apply_discount(100, 150)` computes `discount = 150`, then `100 - 150` panics with 'attempt to subtract with overflow' in a debug build, or wraps to a near-u64::MAX value in a release build.
